hygiene**: update `__manifest__.py` `depends`, `data`, and `version` fields when introducing DB changes or new data files.\n\n**Testing & Local Run**\n- **Where tests live**: `odoo/<module>/tests/` established local development workflow.\n- **Release sanity**: include at least one focused test for new business logic (especially schedule generation, result pipeline, and state transitions).\n\n**PR Checklist (required before merge)**\n- **Tests**: Add/adjust tests covering the new behaviour.\n- **Security**: Update `security/ir.model.access.csv` and add group/record-rule  {"content": "# Workflow: Standings Lifecycle\n\nAutomatic and manual standing recomputation, freeze points, website\npublication, and the impact of official-result changes on standings tables.\n\n## Overview\n\nStandings are derived from results that still have\n`include_in_official_standings = True`. They recompute automatically when a\nresult becomes official, can be recomputed manually at any time, and are\nfrozen when the authoritative ranking for a stage must be locked. Public\nvisibility is separate from the standings state itself and is controlled\nthrough `website_published`.\n\n## Modules Involved\n\n| Module | Role |\n|--------|------|\n| `sports_federation_standings` | Standings model, recompute engine |\n| `sports_federation_result_control` | Result approval triggering recompute |\n| `sports_federation_tournament` | Tournament, stage, match records |\n| `sports_federation_governance` | Override requests for disputed standings |\n| `sports_federation_public_site` | Publication (`website_published`) |\n| `sports_federation_notifications` | Notification on standings publication |\n\n## Models\n\n| Model | Key Fields |\n|-------|-----------|\n| `federation.standings` | `tournament_id`, `stage_id`, `group_id`, `state`, `computed_on`, `website_published`, `public_title` |\n| `federation.standings.line` | `team_id`, `position`, `points`, `played`, `won`, `drawn`, `lost`, `goals_for`, `goals_against`, `goal_diff` |\n\n## Standing States\n\n```\ndraft → computed → frozen\n```\n\n| State | Meaning |\n|-------|---------|\n| `draft` | Standings record exists but has not been computed |\n| `computed` | Standings are up to date with the currently official results |\n| `frozen` | Standings are locked; no further recompute will change them |\n\n`website_published = True` controls whether the standing is visible on the\npublic site. It does not create a separate standings workflow state.\n\n## Step-by-Step Flow\n\n### 1. Automatic Recompute Trigger\n\n**Actor**: System (triggered by result approval)\n**Module**: `sports_federation_result_control` → `sports_federation_standings`\n\nWhen a match result is approved (`result_state = approved`):\n\n1. `include_in_official_standings` is set to `True` on the match record.\n2. The result approval method calls\n   `federation.standings._trigger_recompute(tournament_id, stage_id, group_id)`.\n3. Any `federation.standings` record linked to the same tournament / stage /\n   group that is in `draft` or `computed` state is queued for recompute.\n4. The standings table is rebuilt from scratch from all approved results\n   in that scope.\n5. After recompute, the standings transition to `computed`.\n\n**Frozen standings are not recomputed**. If a result is approved after the\nstandings have been frozen, a warning appears on the match form but the\nstandings are not changed.\n\n### 2. Manual Recompute\n\n**Actor**: Federation administrator\n**Module**: `sports_federation_standings`\n\nWhen results are corrected or the automatic trigger did not fire (e.g. an edge\ncase during bulk import):\n\n1. Navigate to **Federation → Standings** and open the relevant standings record.\n2. Click **Recompute** (only available in `draft` or `computed` states, never on\n   `frozen` or `published`).\n3. The standings engine rebuilds all lines from approved results.\n4. State transitions to `computed`.\n\n### 3. Freeze Decision\n\n**Actor**: Federation administrator (Federation Manager group)\n**Module**: `sports_federation_standings`\n\nStandings are frozen at a natural boundary — end of group stage, end of regular\nseason, or after the last knockout round of a stage:\n\n1. Open the standings record in `computed` state.\n2. Click **Freeze**.\n3. State transitions: `computed → frozen`.\n4. Frozen standings will not be touched by any subsequent result approval in\n   that scope.\n\n**Who can freeze**: only users in the `group_federation_manager` security group\ncan freeze standings.\n\n**When to freeze**: freeze only after all matches in the stage are `done` and\nall results are `approved`. Freezing with unapproved results creates an\nincomplete official table.\n\n### 4. Publication Approval\n\n**Actor**: Federation administrator\n**Module**: `sports_federation_standings` → `sports_federation_public_site`\n\nBefore standings appear on the public website, a publication approval step\nprovides a human review checkpoint:\n\n1. With standings in `computed` or `frozen` state, publish the record from the\n   Website tab.\n2. `website_published` is set to `True`.\n3. The standings page at `/competitions/<edition-slug>/standings` now reflects the\n   table.\n\nIf `sports_federation_notifications` is installed, a notification is dispatched\nto club contacts when standings for their tournament are published.\n\n**Unpublishing**: set `website_published = False` to pull the standings from\nthe public site without changing the `state`. This is useful when a dispute or\nlate correction requires re-review.\n\n### 5. Contested Result Impact on Standings\n\n**Actor**: Club representative or federation official → Governance officer\n**Module**: `sports_federation_result_control` + `sports_federation_governance`\n\nWhen a result is contested after standings have been computed:\n\n1. `result_state` moves to `contested` and\n   `include_in_official_standings` becomes `False`.\n2. Any standings in `draft` or `computed` scope are recomputed automatically\n   and drop the result.\n3. If the standing is `frozen`, federation staff must decide whether to leave\n   the frozen table in place during review or deliberately unfreeze or\n   force-recompute it after governance review.\n4. If the standing is public (`website_published = True`) and the table should\n   be withdrawn during review, unpublish it separately. Publication is not a\n   standings state.\n5. A governance override request may document the review, but it does not keep\n   a contested result official.\n\n## Contested Results and the Frozen Table\n\n| Standing status | Operator action |\n|----------------|-----------------|\n| `draft` / `computed` | Automatic recompute removes the contested result |\n| `frozen` | Federation manager decides whether to unfreeze or force-recompute after review |\n| `website_published = True` | Unpublish separately if the public table should be hidden during review |\n\n## Summary of Access Control\n\n| Action | Required Group |\n|--------|---------------|\n| Manual recompute | `group_federation_manager` |\n| Freeze standings | `group_federation_manager` |\n| Publish / unpublish | `group_federation_manager` |\n| View standings | `group_federation_user` (backend), public (website) |\n\n## Related Workflows\n\n- [WORKFLOW_RESULT_PIPELINE.md](WORKFLOW_RESULT_PIPELINE.md) — Result approval that triggers automatic recompute.\n- [WORKFLOW_APPEAL_DISPUTE.md](WORKFLOW_APPEAL_DISPUTE.md) — Appeal and dispute process for contested results.\n- [WORKFLOW_PUBLIC_PUBLICATION.md](WORKFLOW_PUBLIC_PUBLICATION.md) — Broader public-site publication workflow.\n", "content_length": 6867, "filesystem_mode": "0644", "git_mode": "100644", "git_state": "tracked", "path": "_workflows/WORKFLOW_STANDINGS_LIFECYCLE.md", "record_type": "file", "sha256": "5f4f4090720ce7beaeb793767efd8dae49614b26c3b90434ad07c34f150aa2f3", "size_bytes": 6889}
 {"content": "# Workflow: Tournament Lifecycle\n\nFull lifecycle of a tournament — from competition definition and participant\nenrolment through schedule generation, match execution, and final completion.\n\n## Overview\n\nA **competition** is a recurring series (e.g. \"National League Division 1\").\nWithin each season, competitions host one or more **tournaments** which are\nstructured into stages, groups, and matches. This workflow covers the entire\njourney from initial setup to final completion.\n\nCanonical readiness chain (registration to publication):\n\n1. Confirm season registration.\n2. Confirm tournament participant.\n3. Prepare active ready roster and match-day sheets.\n4. Publish schedule and run live operations.\n5. Approve results.\n6. Recompute/review standings.\n7. Publish tournament and standings surfaces.\n\nBlocking vs warning-only model:\n\n- Blocking: the step cannot proceed (for example, deadline-backed roster blockers\n   or unresolved publication validation blockers).\n- Warning-only: the step can proceed, but requires operator follow-up and may\n   require manager override logging depending on the surface.\n\n## Modules Involved\n\n| Module | Role |\n|--------|------|\n| `sports_federation_base` | Seasons, clubs, teams |\n| `sports_federation_rules` | Rule sets governing scoring, tie-breaks, eligibility |\n| `sports_federation_tournament` | Competition, tournament, stage, group, participant, match models |\n| `sports_federation_competition_core`, `sports_federation_registration` | Competition identity, lifecycle, registration, and participant finalization |\n| `sports_federation_format` | Versioned logical structures and stage graphs |\n| `sports_federation_calendar` | Physical match days, capacity, slots, and timelines |\n| `sports_federation_scheduling` | Deterministic fixture assignment and schedule validation |\n| `sports_federation_schedule_approval` | Schedule review and immutable publication snapshots |\n| `sports_federation_matchday` | Live operations after schedule publication |\n| `sports_federation_venues` | Venue and playing-area assignment |\n| `sports_federation_standings` | Standings computation at each stage |\n| `sports_federation_notifications` | Participant-confirmation and publication notifications |\n| `sports_federation_public_site` | Public publication of tournament pages |\n\n## Verified UI navigation\n\nUse [`docs/COMPETITION_UI_WORKFLOW.md`](../docs/COMPETITION_UI_WORKFLOW.md). The main journey is under **Federation → Competitions → Competition Operations**; addon names below describe ownership, not menu labels.\n\n## Step-by-Step Flow\n\n### 1. Competition Setup\n\n**Actor**: Federation administrator\n**Module**: `sports_federation_rules`, `sports_federation_tournament`\n\n1. Define a **rule set** with scoring values (win/draw/loss points), tie-break\n   criteria, squad-size limits, and eligibility rules.\n2. Create a **competition** (e.g. \"National League Division 1\").\n3. Link the competition to the active season and the rule set.\n4. Set competition state to `active`.\n\n### 2. Tournament Creation\n\n**Actor**: Federation administrator\n**Module**: `sports_federation_tournament`\n\n1. Under the competition, create a **tournament** (e.g. \"NL Div 1 — Season 2025\").\n2. Set tournament type: `league`, `cup`, `friendly`, or `playoff`.\n3. Assign date range, rule set (inherited from competition or overridden).\n4. Set maximum participants if applicable.\n5. If the competition is spread over multiple event days, plan the shared\n   schedule blocks directly on the stage rounds. Each round can carry a\n   calendar date and a venue, while the matches inside that round keep their\n   own kickoff times.\n6. Tournament starts in `draft` state.\n\n### 3. Venue Assignment\n\n**Actor**: Federation administrator\n**Module**: `sports_federation_venues`\n\n1. Create or select venues with address, capacity, and playing areas.\n2. Link venues to the tournament via the `venues` Many2many field.\n3. Individual matches can later reference specific venues and playing areas.\n\n### 4. Participant Enrolment\n\n**Actor**: Federation administrator (or via import)\n**Module**: `sports_federation_tournament`, `sports_federation_import_tools`\n\n1. Add **participants** to the tournament — each links a team to the tournament.\n    - If the flow starts from portal registration requests, an administrator first\n       confirms the `federation.competition.entry` record. That creates or links\n       a `federation.tournament.participant` record in state `registered`.\n    - That participant must still be moved to state `confirmed` before schedule\n       generation can use it.\n2. Optionally assign participants to specific stages and groups.\n3. Set seeding ranks for bracket placement.\n4. Participant states: `registered` → `confirmed` → `withdrawn` / `eliminated`.\n5. Participant confirmation can happen before the team has an active roster, but\n   only until one week before its first scheduled match, or one week before\n   tournament start if no match has been scheduled yet. Once that deadline is\n   reached, participant confirmation is blocked until the team has an active\n   ready roster. When both a competition-specific roster and a season-wide\n   roster are available, the competition-specific roster is used for readiness\n   checks.\n6. The participant form now surfaces the current roster deadline feedback inline\n   and exposes **Open Team Roster** when operators need to resolve the blocker\n   in the rosters flow before confirmation can continue.\n7. Confirming a participant sends an email to the team and club contacts.\n8. Move tournament to `open` state once enrolment is complete.\n\nBulk enrolment is available via the **Import Tournament Participants** wizard.\n\n### 5. Stage & Group Structure\n\n**Actor**: Federation administrator\n**Module**: `sports_federation_tournament`\n\n1. Create **stages** within the tournament (e.g. \"Group Phase\", \"Quarter-Finals\").\n2. Set stage type: `group`, `knockout`, `playoff`, or `other`.\n3. Order stages by sequence.\n4. Within each stage, create **groups** (e.g. \"Group A\", \"Pool 1\").\n5. Assign participants to groups.\n6. Create or review the stage rounds that should exist for each phase. Example:\n   rounds 1-4 for the round-robin stage, then knockout rounds on the final stage.\n\n### 6. Schedule Generation\n\n**Actor**: Federation administrator\n**Modules**: `sports_federation_format`, `sports_federation_calendar`,\n`sports_federation_scheduling`, `sports_federation_schedule_approval`, and\n`sports_federation_matchday`\n\nThe path is an explicit sequence of handovers:\n\n- Freeze the logical structure and stage graph in `sports_federation_format`.\n- Prepare physical match days and playable capacity in\n   `sports_federation_calendar`.\n- Generate or assign fixtures and validate the complete draft in\n   `sports_federation_scheduling`.\n- Submit the draft for review and publish an immutable snapshot through\n   `sports_federation_schedule_approval`.\n- Start live operations only from the published snapshot through\n   `sports_federation_matchday`.\n\n1. Move the competition into the state that permits scheduling.\n2. Registration finalizes and locks the confirmed participant set.\n3. Format freezes the structure and stage graph for the competition edition.\n   Round-robin and knockout generation remain deterministic and scoped to the\n   frozen structure.\n4. Calendar creates match days and `federation.schedule.slot` capacity for the\n   required venues and courts. Slot lifecycle and court timelines are owned by\n   `sports_federation_calendar`.\n5. Scheduling assigns fixtures to available slots, applies fairness and rest\n   validation, and returns a complete draft schedule. Blocking conflicts must be\n   resolved before review; warnings remain visible and auditable.\n6. Schedule approval reviews the draft and publishes an immutable schedule\n   snapshot. Federation managers may approve configured warning-only overrides,\n   with the reason retained in the audit trail.\n7. Match-day operations open and close only published schedules. Referee\n   readiness, venue readiness, result follow-up, and incidents are handled by\n   their owning modules without changing the approved snapshot.\n\n**Round Robin**: The format service generates a complete deterministic pairing\nset where every team plays every other team once or twice according to policy.\n\n**Knockout**: The format service creates a seeded single-elimination bracket,\nincluding byes and future-round wiring for non-power-of-two participant counts.\n\n### 7. Match Execution\n\n**Actor**: Federation staff, referees\n**Module**: `sports_federation_tournament`\n\n1. Matches are scheduled with date/time, venue, home/away teams.\n2. Match states progress: `draft` → `scheduled` → `in_progress` → `done`.\n3. Scores are entered on the match form (home_score, away_score).\n4. Match-day details are handled by the [Match Day Operations](WORKFLOW_MATCH_DAY_OPERATIONS.md)\n   workflow.\n\n### 8. Standings Computation\n\n**Actor**: Federation administrator\n**Module**: `sports_federation_standings`\n\n1. Create a **standings** record scoped to the tournament, stage, or group.\n2. Link the rule set for scoring and tie-break rules.\n3. Compute standings: aggregates match results into ranked lines.\n4. States: `draft` → `computed` → `frozen`.\n5. Frozen standings are the publication candidates for the public site.\n\n### 9. Stage Progression\n\n**Actor**: Federation administrator\n**Module**: `sports_federation_tournament`\n\n1. After a stage completes, review standings to determine qualifiers.\n2. Qualification rules from the rule set indicate who advances.\n3. Use `federation.stage.progression` rules to formalise advancement: these\n   can be single-group, cross-group (e.g. \"best third-placed teams\"), and\n   include seeding/placement strategies. A progression rule can be executed\n   manually (`action_execute()`) or set to `auto_advance=True`.\n    - When designing a versioned structure in Format Studio, use the\n       structure-scoped `federation.structure.stage.progression` edges instead.\n       These graph edges are separate from the competition engine's tournament\n       progression rules and are validated before the structure is generated.\n   - When a standings record is `frozen`/`computed`, any progression rules for\n     that stage with `auto_advance=True` will be executed automatically — new\n     participants are created in the target stage and (optionally) a new stage\n     schedule can be generated automatically.\n4. Tournament templates (`federation.tournament.template`) let administrators\n   scaffold common stage/group/progression combinations (for recurring\n   tournaments). Use `action_apply()` from the template to create stages and\n   progression rules for a tournament in a single step.\n5. Generate the next stage in **Federation → Competitions → Competition Operations → Format Studio**, then assign it in **Schedule Planner**.\n6. Typical workflow: freeze the round-robin standing, auto-advance the top-ranked\n   teams into the knockout stage through a `federation.stage.progression` rule,\n   then schedule those knockout matches onto the planned knockout rounds.\n\n### 10. Tournament Completion\n\n**Actor**: Federation administrator\n**Module**: `sports_federation_tournament`\n\n1. After the final stage, review and approve all remaining results.\n2. Compute and publish final standings.\n3. Set tournament state to `closed`.\n4. Competition can be closed at end of season.\n\n### 11. Public Publication\n\n**Actor**: Federation administrator\n**Module**: `sports_federation_public_site`\n\n1. Set `website_published = True` on the tournament.\n2. Configure public slug, description, and toggle results/standings visibility.\n   The tournament Website tab now states whether publication is blocked because\n   the tournament is still unpublished, standings do not exist yet, or standings\n   remain hidden, and it links back to the standings action when relevant.\n3. Publish standings records. Standings forms also explain whether approved\n   results are still pending or whether website publication is the next valid\n   step.\n4. Participant club and team contacts receive a tournament-publication email the first time the tournament is published.\n5. Public pages become available at `/competitions/<edition-slug>` and the related\n   canonical `/competitions/...` route family.\n\n## State Diagram\n\n```\nCompetition: draft → active → closed\n\nTournament: draft → open → in_progress → closed\n                                       → cancelled\n\nMatch: draft → scheduled → in_progress → done\n                                        → cancelled\n\nStandings: draft → computed → frozen\n\nParticipant: registered → confirmed → withdrawn\n                                    → eliminated\n```\n\n## Key Decision Points\n\n| Question | Outcome |\n|----------|---------|\n| League or Cup format? | Determines round-robin vs. knockout wizard |\n| How many stages? | Single-stage league or multi-stage tournament with progression |\n| Power-of-two bracket? | Knockout wizard handles byes for odd counts |\n| When to publish? | Standings should be computed and verified before publication |\n\n## Related Workflows\n\n- [Match Day Operations](WORKFLOW_MATCH_DAY_OPERATIONS.md) — detailed match-day process\n- [Result Pipeline](WORKFLOW_RESULT_PIPELINE.md) — score verification and approval\n- [Season Registration](WORKFLOW_SEASON_REGISTRATION.md) — prerequisite club/team registration\n", "content_length": 13341, "filesystem_mode": "0644", "git_mode": "100644", "git_state": "tracked", "path": "_workflows/WORKFLOW_TOURNAMENT_LIFECYCLE.md", "record_type": "file", "sha256": "db337c482bba8d3ea106048fd681d349e5f12e1202d1a6f5c3580296a21af355", "size_bytes": 13409}

-{"content": "# ADR-0001: Portal Trust Boundaries\n\nLast updated: 2026-08-20\nOwner: Federation Platform Team\nLast reviewed: 2026-08-20\nReview cadence: Every release\nStatus: Accepted\n\n## Context\n\nPortal club representatives and officials must create or update federation records without receiving broad backend ACLs. Controller-only checks are insufficient because direct model calls, guessed identifiers, or future routes could otherwise widen access.\n\n## Decision\n\nPortal writes use explicit, model-owned privilege boundaries:\n\n- Controllers resolve the request user and the candidate record, reject malformed input, and invoke a model-owned portal method.\n- Ownership and scope are enforced again in the model or shared privilege service.\n- Elevated reads and writes go through `federation.portal.privilege`, including helpers such as `elevate()`, `portal_search()`, `portal_create()`, `portal_write()`, and `portal_call()` where applicable.\n- The privilege boundary preserves the request user for audit attribution while keeping elevation narrow and explicit.\n- Controllers must not perform business writes through raw `sudo()`.\n- Positive in-scope, negative out-of-scope, direct-ID, and elevated-helper tests are mandatory for every privileged portal write surface.\n\n## Consequences\n\n- Privilege escalation remains centralized and reviewable.\n- Controller and ORM boundaries fail closed independently.\n- Cross-club and team-scoped access can be regression-tested consistently.\n- New portal features must reuse the privilege service or add a reviewed model-owned equivalent.\n- Raw elevated controller writes are treated as security defects.\n\n\n## Privileged mutation enforcement\n\nControllers may perform elevated reads only under the documented route and\nownership rules. They must not invoke `sudo().create()`, `sudo().write()`,\n`sudo().unlink()`, or an elevated `action_*()` method directly. Mutations cross\nan owning command service or `federation.portal.privilege`, which repeats the\nscope assertion and records the audit event.\n\n`ci/check_privileged_mutation_boundaries.py` enforces this repository-wide for\nfederation controllers. `ci/check_portal_sudo_guard.py` separately maintains the\nreviewed inventory of portal elevated reads.\n\nDestructive cross-addon deletion uses a process-local object identity and the\nshared context-key constant from\n`sports_federation_base.destructive_tokens`. Only the explicitly reviewed\nmatch-day, scheduling, and publication integrity modules may import that token.\n`ci/check_destructive_token_contract.py` rejects new consumers and raw copies of\nthe context-key string.\n\n\nResult approval and contesting are owned by\n`federation.result.commands`. The command re-resolves the target within the\nactor's current club scope and is the only portal path allowed to supply the\nprocess-local result-transition token. Superuser mode by itself never satisfies\na result role check.\n\n\n## Workflow transition mechanics\n\nOwned command services may delegate common state-transition mechanics to\n`federation.workflow.transition`. The helper is not an HTTP or RPC boundary and\ncontrollers must not call it directly. Eligibility and object scope remain in\nthe owning command service.\n\n\n## Match-day command transactions\n\nControllers and wizards call `federation.matchday.commands`; they do not mutate\noperational records directly. Public command methods establish a savepoint,\nvalidate competition roles, and delegate transition mechanics to\n`federation.workflow.transition`.\n", "content_length": 3484, "filesystem_mode": "0644", "git_mode": "100644", "git_state": "modified", "path": "adr/0001-portal-trust-boundaries.md", "record_type": "file", "sha256": "c4e91c382b2a5ba488e8f7d7cb833e510afe7347b3da01b53ee841d692f1fed5", "size_bytes": 3484}

 {"content": "# ADR-0002: Reporting SQL Views\n\nLast updated: 2026-04-18\nOwner: Federation Platform Team\nLast reviewed: 2026-08-20\nReview cadence: Every release\nStatus: Accepted\n\n## Context\n\nFederation reporting combines finance, standings, compliance, notification, planning, and workflow data across multiple addons. Rebuilding those joins in controllers or repeated ORM loops would duplicate logic and create unpredictable performance.\n\n## Decision\n\nOperational and planning projections remain read-only analytical models backed by PostgreSQL views when their data is naturally cross-module or aggregation-heavy.\n\n- SQL-backed report models use `_auto = False`.\n- View definitions are recreated deterministically from `init()` or the repository's approved view helper.\n- Controllers and exports consume report models instead of embedding substantial SQL or cross-module aggregation logic.\n- Report models are read-only and must not masquerade as writable business records.\n- Heavy reports retain query budgets, representative fixtures, and performance watchpoints.\n- SQL view changes are upgrade-sensitive and require migration review evidence.\n- A normal stored Odoo model is preferred when the data has its own lifecycle or must be edited.\n\n## Consequences\n\n- Cross-module reporting logic remains centralized.\n- Export and operator surfaces share the same projection semantics.\n- View dependencies and upgrade order require explicit review.\n- Maintainers must preserve query plans, migration safety, and read-only behavior.\n", "content_length": 1514, "filesystem_mode": "0644", "git_mode": "100644", "git_state": "tracked", "path": "adr/0002-reporting-sql-views.md", "record_type": "file", "sha256": "ef36c1653fd664b1b66d727fab316472e1dd05aad0b7e71a28d0f01cd5a889ad", "size_bytes": 1514}
 {"content": "# ADR-0003: Public Route Ownership\n\nLast updated: 2026-04-18\nOwner: Federation Platform Team\nLast reviewed: 2026-08-20\nReview cadence: Every release\nStatus: Accepted\n\n## Context\n\nPublic tournament pages, feeds, calendars, registration entry points, and compatibility aliases can collide when several addons define overlapping controllers. Numeric legacy routes also create ambiguity about the canonical public contract.\n\n## Decision\n\n- `/competitions` and `/competitions/<edition-slug>` are the canonical public page routes.\n- Tournament-named page routes are compatibility redirects only.\n\nPublic route ownership is tournament-first and module-explicit:\n\n- `sports_federation_public_site` owns canonical public competition pages and match-day publication views; legacy tournament feeds and calendars remain compatibility contracts.\n- Slug-first routes are canonical for new consumers.\n- Numeric and competition-named routes may remain only as documented compatibility aliases with an owner and review date.\n- Public reads enforce applicable publication controls such as `website_published`, `show_public_results`, and `show_public_standings`.\n- Public write entry points use a model-owned request boundary and must not broaden portal or backend privileges.\n- Route inventory, OpenAPI contracts, compatibility notes, and smoke coverage are part of the ownership boundary.\n- Duplicate or shadow public controllers are removed rather than kept as silent fallbacks.\n\n## Consequences\n\n- Controller precedence and deprecation become reviewable.\n- New public surfaces must update route and contract documentation in the same change.\n- Compatibility routes carry an explicit maintenance cost and sunset decision.\n- Publication defaults remain deny-by-default.\n", "content_length": 1753, "filesystem_mode": "0644", "git_mode": "100644", "git_state": "tracked", "path": "adr/0003-public-route-ownership.md", "record_type": "file", "sha256": "8f2952d166f7cf414b532edcbbe59159565833ea88c150bdc2b4a5248d639a7d", "size_bytes": 1753}

-{"content": "# Match-Day Operations\n\nThis addon executes the current immutable schedule publication. It never edits\napproved publication evidence.\n\n## Operator workflow\n\n- **Match-Day Control** shows readiness and the exact live publication.\n- **Open Match Day** validates the publication digest and creates an immutable\n  execution session.\n- Court status and incidents are changed through command-backed wizards.\n- Operational schedule changes support move, delay, postpone and cancel.\n- Every deviation requires a reason and records the session, publication, actor,\n  old slot and new slot.\n- The immutable `published_slot_id` is preserved. Live reality is represented by\n  `operational_slot_id` and `operational_status`.\n- Normal close requires all matches finished or cancelled and all incidents\n  resolved. Forced close requires a reason.\n\n## Validation\n\n```bash\npython ci/check_schedule_handoff_contract.py\npython ci/check_publication_integrity_contract.py\nbash ci/run_tests.sh --module sports_federation_schedule_approval\nbash ci/run_tests.sh --module sports_federation_matchday\n```\n\n## Restarting unpublished planning\n\nMatch-day managers can use **Restart from Scratch** before any schedule review or\npublication evidence exists. The action requires a reason and explicit destructive\nconfirmation, removes mutable schedules and the old match day, then creates and\nopens a clean replacement with the same edition, date, venue, and slot defaults.\nDirect deletion of a draft match day also removes its draft or change-requested\nworking schedules first. Published, reviewed, open, and closed match days remain\nprotected and must use the normal revision or operational correction workflows.\n\n## Deleting closed test data\n\nFederation managers and match-day managers can use **Delete Match Day** on a\nclosed match day. The confirmation wizard shows the number of schedules,\npublications, execution sessions, deviations, and matches affected. Confirming\nthe deletion permanently removes the match-day planning and execution evidence;\nlinked match records remain in the competition but are detached from the deleted\npublication and calendar slots. The action requires a reason and displays a\nfinal confirmation popup before deletion.\n\n\n\n## Transactional operational commands\n\nMatch-day opening, court status changes, incident resolution, operational match\ndeviations, session closure, and match-day closure use the shared workflow\ntransition service. Every public command runs inside a database savepoint and\nreturns a structured result containing the affected record IDs, actor, and\nresulting state. Forced closure requires a reason. Published schedule evidence\nremains immutable and deviations alter operational fields only.\n\nTransition failures roll back sessions, court statuses, operational match\nchanges, incidents, and audit rows as one unit.\n", "content_length": 2837, "filesystem_mode": "0644", "git_mode": "100644", "git_state": "modified", "path": "sports_federation_matchday/README.md", "record_type": "file", "sha256": "235fd541df3b077c4cce593311c179e194a7b1cec95660d1455230d2d014a024", "size_bytes": 2837}

-{"content": "# Sports Federation Result Control\n\nVersion: 19.0.1.2.0\nOwner: Federation Platform Team\nLast reviewed: 2026-08-20\nReview cadence: Every release\n\nControlled result lifecycle, audit history, separation of duties, and standings officiality for federation matches.\n\n## Workflow\n\nThe result path supports draft, submission, verification, approval, contest, and correction as implemented by the match result controls. Approved results are protected against uncontrolled mutation.\n\n## Safeguards\n\n- submit, verify, and approve permissions are checked at action time\n- separation-of-duties rules prevent forbidden actor reuse\n- approved-score changes require the correction workflow\n- audit rows retain actor, action, and before/after context\n- standings only consume results that meet the officiality rules\n- contested and corrected paths remain traceable\n\n## Integration\n\nPortal and tournament-operation actions call the same model-owned result methods as backend flows. Standings recomputation follows successful official result transitions.\n\n## Tests\n\nCoverage includes lifecycle transitions, immutability, duty separation, contest/correction recovery, audit records, and end-to-end result pipeline tours.\n\n## Removed document\n\n`ROADMAP_RC.md` is deleted. Approved-result immutability is an implemented invariant and belongs in this README and its regression tests, not a permanent mini-roadmap.\n\n\n## Audit evidence protection\n\nAudit evidence is append-only operational history. Normal system and federation\nmanager ACLs do not grant unlink access. Controllers must route elevated\nmutations through an owning command or the portal privilege boundary; static\nrelease checks reject direct controller `sudo()` mutations.\n\n\n## Privileged result commands\n\nPortal approval and contest actions use `federation.result.commands`. The\nservice resolves the match inside the authenticated actor's current club scope,\nthen applies a process-local command token for the elevated domain transition.\nRaw `sudo()` is not authorization and no longer bypasses result role checks.\nBackend submit, verify, approve, contest, correction, and reset actions keep\ntheir existing group and separation-of-duty rules.\n", "content_length": 2185, "filesystem_mode": "0644", "git_mode": "100644", "git_state": "tracked", "path": "sports_federation_result_control/README.md", "record_type": "file", "sha256": "ac76ba9fcc44e2f219968350f4312b0fec6ca12fa8e68828802f65fa3681239a", "size_bytes": 2185}
+{"content": "# Sports Federation Result Control\n\nVersion: 19.0.1.2.0\nOwner: Federation Platform Team\nLast reviewed: 2026-08-20\nReview cadence: Every release\n\nControlled result lifecycle, audit history, separation of duties, and standings officiality for federation matches.\n\n## Workflow\n\nThe result path supports draft, submission, verification, approval, contest, and correction as implemented by the match result controls. Approved results are protected against uncontrolled mutation.\n\n## Safeguards\n\n- submit, verify, and approve permissions are checked at action time\n- separation-of-duties rules prevent forbidden actor reuse\n- approved-score changes require the correction workflow\n- audit rows retain actor, action, and before/after context\n- standings only consume results that meet the officiality rules\n- contested and corrected paths remain traceable\n\n## Integration\n\nPortal and tournament-operation actions call the same model-owned result methods as backend flows. Standings recomputation follows successful official result transitions.\n\n## Tests\n\nCoverage includes lifecycle transitions, immutability, duty separation, contest/correction recovery, audit records, and end-to-end result pipeline tours.\n\n## Removed document\n\n`ROADMAP_RC.md` is deleted. Approved-result immutability is an implemented invariant and belongs in this README and its regression tests, not a permanent mini-roadmap.\n\n\n## Audit evidence protection\n\nAudit evidence is append-only operational history. Normal system and federation\nmanager ACLs do not grant unlink access. Controllers must route elevated\nmutations through an owning command or the portal privilege boundary; static\nrelease checks reject direct controller `sudo()` mutations.\n\n\n## Privileged result commands\n\nPortal approval and contest actions use `federation.result.commands`. The\nservice resolves the match inside the authenticated actor's current club scope,\nthen applies a process-local command token for the elevated domain transition.\nRaw `sudo()` is not authorization and no longer bypasses result role checks.\nBackend submit, verify, approve, contest, correction, and reset actions keep\ntheir existing group and separation-of-duty rules.\n\n\n## Transactional result lifecycle\n\nSubmission, verification, approval, contesting, correction, and reset use the\nshared workflow transition foundation. Every action locks the match row, runs\nin a database savepoint, returns a structured command result, preserves the\nresult-specific audit trail, and emits a common workflow-transition audit event.\nSeparation of duties is expressed as forbidden actor fields for verification\nand approval.\n", "content_length": 2626, "filesystem_mode": "0644", "git_mode": "100644", "git_state": "tracked", "path": "sports_federation_result_control/README.md", "record_type": "file", "sha256": "304fe26a82c4946ff4afffbabdf93c314d40d68b7af970dce36dcd1358bcb409", "size_bytes": 2626}

 {"content": "Sports Federation Rosters\n=========================\n\nSeason and competition-bound team rosters plus match-day squad sheets. Controls\nwhich players are eligible and available for each match, enforces squad-size\nlimits from the applicable rule set, and surfaces operator-readable readiness\nfeedback before rosters, participants, or match sheets move forward.\n\nPurpose\n-------\n\nProvides a formal roster, which is the pool of players a team may select from\nfor a season or competition, and match sheets, which are the specific squad and\nstarting lineup for an individual match. The module links to rule sets for\nsquad-size validation and to the shared eligibility service for license,\nregistration, and suspension checks.\n\nDependencies\n------------\n\n- ``sports_federation_base``: Clubs, teams, and seasons.\n- ``sports_federation_people``: Players.\n- ``sports_federation_tournament``: Tournaments and matches.\n- ``sports_federation_rules``: Squad-size limits and player eligibility checks.\n- ``mail``: Chatter integration.\n\nModels\n------\n\n``federation.team.roster``\n~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~\n\nA pool of eligible players for a team within a season or competition scope.\n\nFields:\n\n- ``name`` (Char): Generated roster label.\n- ``team_id`` (Many2one): Team.\n- ``season_id`` (Many2one): Season scope.\n- ``season_registration_id`` (Many2one): Linked registration.\n- ``competition_id`` (Many2one): Optional competition scope.\n- ``rule_set_id`` (Many2one): Squad-size rules.\n- ``status`` (Selection): ``draft``, ``active``, or ``closed``.\n- ``valid_from`` / ``valid_to`` (Date): Validity window.\n- ``line_ids`` (One2many): Rostered players.\n- ``line_count`` (Integer): Player count.\n- ``club_id`` (Many2one, computed): Derived from the team.\n- ``min_players_required`` / ``max_players_allowed`` (Integer): Limits pulled\n   from the rule set.\n- ``ready_for_activation`` (Boolean, computed): Whether activation checks pass.\n- ``readiness_feedback`` (Text, computed): Aggregated activation blockers.\n- ``match_sheet_count`` (Integer, computed): Linked match sheets using this\n   roster.\n- ``match_day_locked`` (Boolean, computed): Whether live match sheets now lock\n   roster scope changes.\n- ``match_day_lock_feedback`` (Text, computed): Why the roster scope is locked.\n- ``audit_event_ids`` (One2many): Participation audit events for this roster.\n\n``federation.team.roster.line``\n~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~\n\nA single player entry on a roster.\n\nFields:\n\n- ``roster_id`` (Many2one): Parent roster.\n- ``player_id`` (Many2one): The player.\n- ``status`` (Selection): ``active``, ``inactive``, ``suspended``, or\n   ``removed``.\n- ``date_from`` / ``date_to`` (Date): Availability window.\n- ``jersey_number`` (Char): Squad number.\n- ``is_captain`` / ``is_vice_captain`` (Boolean): Leadership flags.\n- ``license_id`` (Many2one): Explicit season license to validate.\n- ``eligible`` (Boolean, computed): Current eligibility status.\n- ``eligibility_feedback`` (Text, computed): Human-readable failure reasons.\n- ``notes`` (Text): Remarks.\n\nKey behaviour:\n\n- Once a submitted, approved, or locked match sheet references a roster line,\n   that referenced line cannot be structurally changed or removed.\n\n``federation.match.sheet``\n~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~\n\nThe squad list submitted for a specific match.\n\nFields:\n\n- ``name`` (Char): Sheet title.\n- ``match_id`` (Many2one): The match.\n- ``team_id`` (Many2one): Which team the sheet belongs to.\n- ``roster_id`` (Many2one): Source roster.\n- ``side`` (Selection): ``home`` or ``away``.\n- ``state`` (Selection): ``draft``, ``submitted``, ``approved``, or ``locked``.\n- ``line_ids`` (One2many): Player entries.\n- ``line_count`` (Integer): Squad size.\n- ``ready_for_submission`` (Boolean, computed): Whether submission checks pass.\n- ``readiness_feedback`` (Text, computed): Aggregated submission blockers.\n- ``substitution_count`` (Integer, computed): Number of recorded substitution\n   entries.\n- ``locked_on`` / ``locked_by_id`` (Datetime / Many2one): Final lock metadata.\n- ``audit_event_ids`` (One2many): Participation audit events for this sheet.\n- ``coach_name`` / ``manager_name`` (Char): Team staff.\n- ``notes`` (Text): Remarks.\n\nState machine:\n\n- ``draft -> submitted -> approved -> locked``.\n- Submitted sheets may return to draft for operator corrections before\n   approval.\n- Matches created interactively receive draft home and away sheets when the\n   rosters module is installed. Demo data loading runs without this side\n   effect, so explicit fixtures such as the demo pack can define their own\n   sheets without colliding with automatically created records.\n\n``federation.match.sheet.line``\n~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~\n\nA player on a match sheet.\n\nFields:\n\n- ``match_sheet_id`` (Many2one): Parent sheet.\n- ``player_id`` (Many2one): The player.\n- ``roster_line_id`` (Many2one): Source roster line.\n- ``is_starter`` (Boolean): In the starting lineup.\n- ``is_substitute`` (Boolean): Bench selection.\n- ``is_captain`` (Boolean): Match captain.\n- ``jersey_number`` (Char): Shirt number.\n- ``entered_minute`` / ``left_minute`` (Integer): Substitution timeline\n   tracking.\n- ``eligible`` (Boolean, computed): Current eligibility status.\n- ``eligibility_feedback`` (Text, computed): Human-readable failure reasons.\n- ``notes`` (Text): Remarks.\n\n``federation.participation.audit``\n~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~\n\nImmutable operational log for roster and match-sheet activity.\n\nFields:\n\n- ``event_type`` (Selection): Created, updated, submitted, approved, locked,\n   and substitution events.\n- ``team_id`` (Many2one): Team owning the event.\n- ``roster_id`` (Many2one): Related season roster when applicable.\n- ``match_sheet_id`` (Many2one): Related match sheet when applicable.\n- ``match_id`` (Many2one): Related match when applicable.\n- ``player_id`` (Many2one): Player affected by the event.\n- ``description`` (Text): Human-readable audit detail.\n- ``author_id`` / ``event_on`` (Many2one / Datetime): Attribution and\n   timestamp.\n\n``federation.tournament.participant`` Extension\n~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~\n\nThis module extends tournament participants with team-linked roster readiness\nchecks. Tournament registration auto-provisions a team roster for the relevant\nseason and competition scope. Participants can still be confirmed and assigned\nwithout a ready roster before the roster deadline, but once that deadline is\nreached both participant confirmation and scheduled matches require an active\nready roster: one week before the first scheduled match, or one week before the\ntournament start if no match has been scheduled yet.\n\nFields:\n\n- ``ready_for_confirmation`` (Boolean, computed): Whether the linked team\n   currently satisfies the roster deadline rule.\n- ``roster_deadline_date`` (Date, computed): Deadline for having an active\n   ready roster.\n- ``readiness_roster_id`` (Many2one, computed): Preferred team roster used for\n   readiness checks.\n- ``confirmation_feedback`` (Text, computed): Warning or blocking message about\n   the roster deadline.\n\nKey Behaviours\n--------------\n\n- **Roster scoping**: rosters are tied to a season and optionally a\n   competition, preventing cross-competition player sharing.\n- **Eligibility-aware activation**: roster activation is blocked until active\n   lines satisfy date windows, squad-size bounds, and shared eligibility rules.\n- **Readable operator feedback**: roster lines and match-sheet lines expose\n   ``eligibility_feedback``, while rosters and match sheets aggregate blockers\n   into readiness summaries.\n- **Match sheet from roster**: match sheets validate against explicit roster\n   lines so team, date-window, and license mismatches are caught early.\n- **Match-day locking**: submitted and approved sheet activity locks roster\n   scope changes and the referenced roster lines so historical lineups remain\n   defensible.\n- **Undoable closure**: closing a roster is no longer terminal. Federation\n   staff can reopen a closed roster back to active when closure was premature,\n   while active-roster uniqueness and readiness checks still apply.\n- **Substitution governance**: approved sheets can record ``entered_minute``\n   and ``left_minute`` values while still blocking lineup changes after\n   approval.\n- **Participation audit trail**: roster lifecycle changes, lineup changes,\n   submissions, submitted-sheet resets, approvals, locks, and substitutions are\n   captured in ``federation.participation.audit``.\n- **Participant roster readiness**: tournament registration creates or reuses\n   the relevant team roster automatically so roster maintenance stays attached\n   to the participating team instead of requiring a separately named setup step.\n- **Operational roster deadline**: tournament participants can still be\n   confirmed and grouped without a ready roster before the deadline, but once\n   the one-week deadline is reached operators cannot confirm participants or\n   schedule matches until an active ready roster exists.\n- **Guided roster handoff**: confirmed season registrations now open the roster\n   list with the relevant team, season, competition, and rule-set context, and\n   participant forms expose the current roster deadline plus an `Open Team\n   Roster` handoff when readiness work is the next blocker.\n- **Team-linked roster checks**: team roster lookup and tournament deadline\n   assessment are owned by the team model so roster compliance follows the team\n   rather than being treated as a separate participant-only concern.\n- **State locking**: approved match sheets can be locked once match-day\n   operations are complete.\n\n\n## Audit evidence protection\n\nAudit evidence is append-only operational history. Normal system and federation\nmanager ACLs do not grant unlink access. +FILE: ci/check_result_transition_contract.py
+SIZE: 3507

+SHA256: 958e81c3d3a44ed0ddc50dbd091c726e7c3ac6779db6ac1b851caaed9e588c33

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Protect result workflow transaction, locking, and transition contracts."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import ast
+from pathlib import Path
+import sys
+
+ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
+MODEL = ROOT / "sports_federation_result_control/models/match_result_control.py"
+COMMANDS = ROOT / "sports_federation_result_control/services/result_commands.py"
+ACTIONS = {
+    "action_submit_result",
+    "action_verify_result",
+    "action_approve_result",
+    "action_contest_result",
+    "action_correct_result",
+    "action_reset_result_to_draft",
+}
+EVENTS = {"submitted", "verified", "approved", "contested", "corrected", "reset"}
+
+
+def methods(path: Path) -> dict[str, ast.FunctionDef]:
+    tree = ast.parse(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"), filename=str(path))
+    result = {}
+    for node in ast.walk(tree):
+        if isinstance(node, ast.FunctionDef):
+            result[node.name] = node
+    return result
+
+
+def find_violations(root: Path = ROOT) -> list[str]:
+    model = root / MODEL.relative_to(ROOT)
+    commands = root / COMMANDS.relative_to(ROOT)
+    if not model.is_file():
+        return ["result-control model is missing"]
+    if not commands.is_file():
+        return ["result command service is missing"]
+    source = model.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
+    command_source = commands.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
+    found = methods(model)
+    violations = []
+    for action in sorted(ACTIONS):
+        method = found.get(action)
+        if not method:
+            violations.append(f"result action is missing: {action}")
+            continue
+        fragment = ast.get_source_segment(source, method) or ""
+        if "savepoint()" not in fragment:
+            violations.append(f"{action} is not transactionally savepoint-bound")
+        if "_lock_result_transition()" not in fragment:
+            violations.append(f"{action} does not lock the result row")
+        if "_result_transition(" not in fragment:
+            violations.append(f"{action} bypasses the shared transition helper")
+    missing_events = sorted(
+        event for event in EVENTS if f'event_type="{event}"' not in source
+    )
+    if missing_events:
+        violations.append(f"result transition events are missing: {missing_events}")
+    for direct in (
+        '"result_state": "submitted"',
+        '"result_state": "verified"',
+        '"result_state": "approved"',
+        '"result_state": "contested"',
+        '"result_state": "corrected"',
+        '"result_state": "draft"',
+    ):
+        if direct in source:
+            violations.append(f"direct result-state mutation remains: {direct}")
+    command_methods = methods(commands)
+    for portal_method in ("approve_portal_result", "contest_portal_result"):
+        method = command_methods.get(portal_method)
+        if not method:
+            violations.append(f"portal result command is missing: {portal_method}")
+            continue
+        fragment = ast.get_source_segment(command_source, method) or ""
+        if "savepoint()" not in fragment:
+            violations.append(f"{portal_method} lacks a transactional savepoint")
+    return violations
+
+
+def main() -> int:
+    violations = find_violations()
+    if violations:
+        print("Result transition contract failed:", file=sys.stderr)
+        for violation in violations:
+            print(f"- {violation}", file=sys.stderr)
+        return 1
+    print("Result transition contract passed.")
+    return 0
+
+
 if __name__ == "__main__":
     raise SystemExit(main())

 Backend submit, verify, approve, contest, correction, and reset actions keep
 their existing group and separation-of-duty rules.
 
+
+## Transactional result lifecycle
+
+Submission, verification, approval, contesting, correction, and reset use the
+shared workflow transition foundation. Every action locks the match row, runs
+in a database savepoint, returns a structured command result, preserves the
+result-specific audit trail, and emits a common workflow-transition audit event.
+Separation of duties is expressed as forbidden actor fields for verification
+and approval.

+    def _result_transition(
+        self,
+        target_state,
+        allowed_from,
+        values=None,
+        reason=False,
+        reason_required=False,
+        forbidden_actor_fields=None,
+        event_type=False,
+        description=False,
+    ):
+        """Apply shared mechanics while preserving the result-specific audit."""
+        results = []
+        transition = self.env["federation.workflow.transition"]
+        for record in self:
+            previous_state = record.result_state
+            transition_reason = reason(record) if callable(reason) else reason
+            result = transition.execute(
+                record,
+                target_state,
+                allowed_from,
+                values=values(record) if callable(values) else values,
+                state_field="result_state",
+                reason=transition_reason,
+                reason_required=reason_required,
+                forbidden_actor_fields=forbidden_actor_fields,
+                event_type=event_type,
+                description=description,
+            )
+            record._log_result_audit(
+                event_type,
+                description,
+                previous_state,
+                target_state,
+                reason=transition_reason,
+            )
+            results.append(result)
+        return {
+            "record_model": self._name,
+            "record_ids": self.ids,
+            "current_state": target_state,
+            "actor_id": self.env.user.id,
+            "results": results,
+        }

+            type(transition),
+            "execute",
+            side_effect=RuntimeError("injected result transition failure"),
+        ), self.assertRaises(RuntimeError):
+            self.match.with_user(self.submitter_user).action_submit_result()
+        self.assertEqual(self.match.result_state, "draft")
+        self.assertFalse(self.match.result_submitted_by_id)
+        self.assertFalse(self.match.result_audit_ids)
+
+    def test_workflow_transition_audit_covers_complete_result_lifecycle(self):
+        self.match.with_user(self.submitter_user).action_submit_result()
+        self.match.with_user(self.verifier_user).action_verify_result()
+        self.match.with_user(self.approver_user).action_approve_result()
+        self.match.result_contest_reason = "Lifecycle audit contest"
+        self.match.action_contest_result()
+        self.match.result_correction_reason = "Lifecycle audit correction"
+        self.match.action_correct_result()
+        self.match.with_user(self.approver_user).action_reset_result_to_draft()
+        events = self.env["federation.audit.event"].search(
+            [
+                ("event_family", "=", "workflow_transition"),
+                ("target_model", "=", "federation.match"),
+                ("target_res_id", "=", self.match.id),
+            ]
+        )
+        self.assertEqual(
+            set(events.mapped("event_type")),
+            {
+                "submitted",
+                "verified",
+                "approved",
+                "contested",
+                "corrected",
+                "reset",
+            },
+        )
